0.x: **Mahendravarman I**, son of **Simhavishnu**: titles **Mattavilasa, Vichitrachitta, Gunabhara, Chitrakarapuli, Lalitankura**; **Vatapikonda** belongs to Narasimhavarman I.

r: Began as a **Jain** → turned **Shaiva** under **Appar (Tirunavukkarasar)**, not Sambandar
South Indian rock-cut temples begin with him – **Mandagapattu** (no brick, timber, metal or mortar)
**Kudumiamalai** music inscription credited to his patronage
With **Pulakesin II** began under him; lost the Krishna-Godavari lands (Maruturu, Kopparam records)
**The bull (Nandi)** – tiger = Chola, boar = Chalukya, fish = Pandya
Parthian (Pahlava), **Andhra** (early Prakrit charters from the Krishna-Guntur region; replaced the Ikshvakus) and local Tamil – not Scythian

1.x: Charters and the end of the Ikshvakus

r: Prakrit; among the earliest Pallava records
Pallava conquest of **Vijayapuri**: the **Pallavas replaced the Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri**

1.x: **Downfall of the Ikshvakus = the Pallavas**: Simhavarman defeated the **last Ikshvaku Rudrapurushadatta**.

r: Founder of the imperial line; **defeated the Kalabhras**
Wars with Pulakesin II; lost the northern (Krishna-Godavari) lands
**Defeated by Vikramaditya II**; Kanchi captured for a time
Killed by **Aditya I Chola** (c. 897; some say 903) – end

2.x: **Order:** Simhavishnu → **Mahendravarman I → Narasimhavarman I → Paramesvaravarman I** → Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) → **Nandivarman II**; **later rulers:** Dantivarman, Nandivarman III, Nripatunga, **Aparajita**.
Cross-dynasty order: **Mahendravarman I (c. 600) → Gopala (Pala, c. 750) → Bhoja (Pratihara, 836) → Parantaka I (Chola, 907)**.

r: A **boy of 12** from a **collateral line**, **chosen by ministers, nobles and people** after Paramesvaravarman II died (c. 731)
Ardent **Vaishnava**; built **Vaikuntha Perumal, Kanchi**; contemporary of **Tirumangai Alvar**
**Brahminical (Vedic) college** / settlement of Brahmin scholars – **Hindu colleges**; usually **attached to temples**; **Sanskrit** medium
**Vishnukundins** and **Eastern Chalukya Jayasimha I** (Asanapura ghatika) also set up ghatikas
Brahmin student at the **Kanchi Ghatika**, insulted by a **Pallava horseman** → founded the **Kadamba** kingdom (**Talagunda inscription**)

3.x: **Hiuen Tsang** visited Kanchi **c. 640 CE**, under Narasimhavarman I.
**Grantha** script of the Pallavas = parent of Southeast Asian scripts; the Pallavas pioneered **Dravida** temple art.

r: **Two naval expeditions to Ceylon** (c. 642 onwards) to restore his ally **Manavarma**
Hiuen Tsang visited Kanchi in his reign
